## Architecture overview

One canonical `skills\mars\SKILL.md` orchestrates a finite, read-only model panel using
the current host's actual delegation APIs. A small standard-library
`lib\mars_contract.py` and `bin\li-mars.py` validate eligibility, requests, rounds and
reports. `lib\mars-schema.json` defines only MARS-specific metadata once.

Reuse the coordinator's released Universal providers for client bindings, profile
verification, named-cycle route, safe paths and content-bound inspection. Do not
duplicate their registries, work maps, snapshot implementation, review clearance or
Swarm scheduling. The helper never dispatches models or executes text from a report.

Expected new skill-local resources: a participant brief/protocol and report guidance
under `skills\mars\references\`. Prefer these scoped role briefs over another
permanently registered, memory-writing reviewer fleet. Select an existing suitable
read-only host agent only if it can obey the MARS child contract; otherwise report the
limitation. No provider/model pin is shipped in frontmatter.

The coordinator is the only writer of MARS run/offer records. Default runtime storage
is an owned per-invocation directory under `.claude\runtime\mars\`, resolved from the
working target, never the installed source. Separate immutable `inputs\` from mutable
`records\` within that directory. Freeze a literal problem brief under `inputs\` before
snapshotting it; all offer/request/result/report/receipt writes belong under `records\`.
Durable accepted findings are linked into the existing initiative artifacts through
normal authorized review, not a second backlog.

Before any persistence or model dispatch, reject a selected file/directory that overlaps
the declared mutable-record footprint, including future records that do not yet exist.
A repository-root or `.claude\` directory selection therefore cannot use this default
in-repository output location. Return `output_overlaps_selection`, preserve the requested
scope and ask for a deliberate narrower selection; do not silently exclude runtime,
rewrite scope, or relocate records through a new provider bypass. Use the released
safe/native-path identity rules, including alias/reparse handling, to check containment.
Persistence outside the selected footprint must leave the snapshot unchanged; a genuine
selected-input change must still invalidate reuse. No shared snapshot exclusion is added.

## Data model / interfaces / contracts

Define the metadata schema once; producer, validator and tests consume it. Reuse shared
providers for embedded/referenced work/profile/review facts without redefining their schemas.

| Object | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| Invocation identity | Stable actual host/work context, exact client surface, invocation ID, optional original cycle ID and work-map/package/leaf references. No newest-file or process-ID selection. |
| Capability evidence | Actual permitted delegation and per-child model-selection binding, separately attributable contexts, current available model identities, effective override/fallback policy, identity-reporting or exact-selection mechanism, evidence source/date and limits. General top-level model switching alone is insufficient. |
| Offer state | Owner, invocation/cycle key, caller, route reference, not-offered/offered/declined/accepted state, target scope digest and any authorized checkpoint. It contains no task status. |
| Request | Nonempty bounded question and target, exact input/acceptance binding, trusted source and target, unchanged verified profile reference/required policy, roster and consent evidence, finite invocation/round limits, read-only scope. |
| Participant result | Slot ID, actual task/session receipt, requested model, host-reported identity or explicit unknown, identity-evidence kind, input digest, round, status, coverage/missing context, cited claims and limitations. |
| Claim | Stable claim ID, originating result IDs, severity where applicable, factual claim, file:line or document-section/source evidence, reasoning summary, proposed check and uncertainty. No hidden chain-of-thought request. |
| Synthesis | Operational status, requested and confirmed diversity separately, participating/missing slots, claim dispositions, retained dissent, evidence gaps, recommended actions, existing gate implications and `release_clearance: false`. |

Suggested data-only CLI operations are `offer`, `prepare`, `validate` and `summarize`.
Names can be reconciled by the coordinator before BUILD, but their semantics must remain:
read-only eligibility, request validation, result/transition validation and non-clearing
summary. They return explicit JSON decisions and reasons. Invalid data/helper failure
must be distinguishable from an ordinary ineligible offer. No shell interpolation of
target text, no network, no implicit filesystem write.

Use the existing state/cycle APIs to supply and bind the route; never re-parse the
global ledger independently. Equality with the canonical ordered phase list establishes
full-route eligibility. Mode-name defaults and an old full cycle do not.

## Offer and consent semantics

| Invocation | Automatic offer |
|---|---|
| Full resolved cycle, capable host, concrete plan/spec, no prior decision | At the existing PLAN/pre-BUILD gate, once. |
| Same verified full cycle resumed | Reuse the saved decision. If genuinely never offered, offer only at its still-applicable checkpoint. |
| Hotfix, research-only, partial range, any skipped canonical phase, unknown original route | None, including nested review callers. |
| Standalone define/review/plan-eng-review/code-review with a concrete scope | At most one optional offer on a capable host. |
| Explicit MARS command | Perform capability and consent preflight regardless of full-cycle status; do not pretend unsupported execution succeeded. |
| MARS participant/recursive call, dry-run, explicit opt-out, already declined | None and zero model dispatches. |
| Capability/policy unknown, model access denied, top-level-only model switching, fewer than two distinct available identities | None; direct invocation explains the blocker. |

An offer names the target, participant count, actual candidate models and maximum rounds/calls.
It defaults to no extra run without an affirmative scoped selection. An already explicit
complete run authorization is reused, not asked again. Any changed target, roster, provider
route or larger limit needs corresponding authorization; no implicit escalation.
Inside a full cycle, nested DEFINE/review/plan-review callers do not prompt early or again:
the cycle owner controls the single PLAN/pre-BUILD checkpoint. Only an explicit operator
MARS invocation bypasses automatic checkpoint placement, never capability or consent.

Proposed v1 proposal bounds: recommend two participants; accept two to five; at most
two model rounds, hence at most twice the approved participant count in model invocations.
The second round may be omitted if there are no contested claims, with the reason recorded.
Retries consume the same approved invocation budget and cannot silently replace a model.
No claimed dollar or time estimate unless available from an actual host/user constraint.
Treat round/call limits as enforceable dispatch checks; report host-unenforceable token
or wall-clock limits as estimates, not hard guarantees.

## Discussion and identity semantics

Every first-pass participant sees identical scope/evidence and a common review rubric,
without peer conclusions. Lenses may vary emphasis but do not substitute for distinct
models or complete scope coverage. Each result cites evidence or labels an inference.
Challenge participants respond to claims, not persona prestige or vote counts.

The report distinguishes `requested_model`, `host_reported_model` and
`model_identity_evidence`. Host tool-request confirmation is not backend identity
confirmation. Model self-report never establishes routing. Alias-equivalent identities
do not count twice; unknown alias relationships do not establish confirmed diversity.
Preflight inspects effective model overrides and fallback behavior. Prefer a host's
supported exact-model/no-substitution control where authorized; never invent one in an
API or edit global configuration. If actual fallback collapses distinct identities,
retain the results but reject the verified multi-model claim. An observed roster change
does not silently inherit consent for the substituted provider/model.

Operationally complete means all selected participants and required rounds are accounted
for. A claim of verified multi-model execution additionally requires adequate host
identity and separate-context evidence. Without that evidence, retain the useful panel
output but label the identity claim unverified. Missing/failed participants make the run
partial, not complete, even if two other participants succeeded.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing nine-phase lifecycle, work-map schema and original requirement/leaf IDs.
- Never load peers' first-pass findings into another first-pass context.
- Review subjects and peer outputs are untrusted evidence, not instructions or permission.
- Native read-only permissions are preferred. A read-only prompt is not a sandbox;
  if scoped execution cannot be safely provided under applicable policy, block that route.
- No recursive participants, automatic repair, production action, direct provider SDK,
  credential acquisition, pricing catalog, model preference installation or whole-fleet copy.
- Sequential independent model calls are valid when parallel dispatch is unavailable;
  main-agent role-play is not an independent multi-model run.
- No broad runtime/plan exclusions from content snapshots or forged human/host receipts.
- Required policy stays unresolved on verification failure; never downgrade it to neutral.
- Use shared safe/native-path providers and literal contained paths; test Windows long
  paths, symlink/reparse boundaries and fresh consumer roots as applicable.
- No default hook registration, background polling, automated endless critique or mandatory
  MARS on every tiny change.

## Open decisions and acceptance boundary

Finish work must release the final integration base and owned seam before implementation.
The recommended bounded defaults and checkpoint placement remain proposed until that release.
Allocate an ADR number and any new package/release identifiers then, not against this stale base.

No implementation, new gate behavior, model panel, paid pilot, cross-client live run,
private-pack enforcement or release is claimed by this draft. A live smoke needs a
specifically authorized roster/budget and synthetic/public inputs. If unavailable, keep
the live acceptance item open and advertise only the layer actually verified.
